evidence.description: Analytics is declared as an open actor.

candidates.explanation: Swift actors cannot be subclassed and cannot be declared open. This declaration is invalid Swift.
candidates.title: Actor declared with unsupported open access

evidence.description: The selected endpoint is passed to NetworkConfiguration using a force unwrap without a preceding nil check.

candidates.explanation: The endpoint is optional, but this function does not establish that it contains a value. If the selected URL provider endpoint is nil, constructing the network configuration traps.
candidates.title: Optional network endpoint is force-unwrapped

evidence.description: The nonisolated setting can be changed independently of the Analytics actor.
Endpoint selection and authentication selection read the mutable setting separately.

candidates.explanation: makeNetworkConfig reads shouldUseMicroInstance twice without an atomic snapshot. A concurrent setter can change the value between those reads, producing a configuration with the normal endpoint and micro-instance authentication headers, or the micro endpoint without those headers. Actor isolation does not serialize this nonisolated setting with configuration construction.
candidates.title: Concurrent configuration changes can mismatch endpoint and authentication

evidence.description: The common tracking method excludes the SDK tracking call when TESTING is defined.
The usage-data settings method invokes the SDK directly without the testing-build condition.

candidates.explanation: When TESTING is defined, ordinary event tracking is suppressed, but sendAnonymousUsageDataSetting still invokes tracker.track. This leaves a tracking path active in the same build configuration that explicitly disables the common path.
candidates.title: Settings tracking bypasses the testing-build suppression
